{{Recipe summary
| Category = Soup recipes
| Servings = 2-3
| Time = 35-50 minutes
| Difficulty = 2
| Image = [[File:Oghwoevwri (Oghwo Evwri).jpg|Oghwoevwri_(Oghwo_Evwri)|300px]]
}}

{{Recipe}}

'''Owo soup''', also known as '''oghwo ofigbo''' or '''ogwofibo''', is a traditional soup native to southern Nigeria.
 
==Ingredients==
* Fresh [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]]
* Fresh pepper
* 500 g [[Cookbook:Goat|goat]] meat, bushmeat, or assorted meat, washed
* 1 small [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* Seasoning/[[Cookbook:Bouillon Cube|stock cubes]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* 1 handful [[Cookbook:Dryfish|dried fish]], washed with hot water
* [[Cookbook:Ground Crayfish|Ground crayfish]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Potash|potash]] (akaun), ground to a powder
* [[Cookbook:Palm Oil|Palm oil]]

==Procedure==
# Blend the tomatoes and pepper to a paste.
# Combine the meat, onions, seasoning cube, and salt in a pot. Cook for about 3 minutes in its own juices.
# Cover meat with water, and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] until tender.
# Add the dried fish, tomato-pepper paste, and ground crayfish to the meat. Add about a cup of water and stir. Let simmer for 10 minutes, stirring to prevent burning.
# Dissolve the potash powder in 4 tablespoons of hot water. Strain the mixture carefully, and mix the liquid into the soup.
# Turn off the heat, and allow the soup to cool for about 10 minutes.
# Return to the heat, and gradually stir in the palm oil.
# Remove from the heat, and serve with [[Cookbook:Plantain|plantains]], [[Cookbook:Yam|yam]], or any [[Cookbook:Swallow|swallow]] of choice.
